abstract: With the wide application of graph neural network (GNN) in many fields, how to extract and aggregate node features effectively has become a hot research issue. In this paper, we propose a graph neural network algorithm that leverages graph convolution and the attention mechanism to enhance the expressive power and aggregation efficacy of node features within a single subgraph. The model's core framework comprises two primary steps: Firstly, node features are extracted from subgraphs utilizing the graph convolution algorithm. In particular, the graph convolution operation updates the feature representation of each node by disseminating information from its adjacent nodes. This process can capture local structural information and effectively integrate the neighborhood features of nodes, thus enhancing the semantic representation of features. Secondly, using the extracted node features, the model incorporates an attention mechanism to aggregate the features in a weighted manner. By evaluating the similarity between each node and its neighboring nodes, the attention mechanism is able to dynamically assign weights to various nodes, thereby emphasizing the significance of key nodes during the aggregation process. This method overcomes the limitation of treating all neighbor nodes equally in the traditional aggregation method, and can more accurately reflect the relevance and importance of the nodes in the subgraph. The experimental outcomes show that the proposed algorithm outperforms existing techniques in terms of performance across various graph datasets.

articleTitle: Research on Target Tracking Control of Soccer Robots Based on Fuzzy Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 5th International Conference on Power, Electronics and Computer Applications (ICPECA)
abstract: With the continuous development of soccer robot technology, target tracking control has become one of its core technologies. Traditional target tracking methods often exhibit poor robustness and flexibility when facing complex and dynamic environments. To address this issue, this paper proposes a target tracking control method for soccer robots based on fuzzy algorithms. By introducing a fuzzy logic controller, this study effectively handles the uncertainty of targets and the dynamic changes of the environment. First, the kinematic model of the soccer robot is analyzed, and a fuzzy controller suitable for target tracking requirements is designed. Second, the proposed method is validated through experiments and simulations, demonstrating superior performance in terms of tracking accuracy, response speed, and robustness compared to traditional PID control and model predictive control methods. Finally, the limitations of the method are discussed, and directions for future improvements are proposed. The research results show that the target tracking control method based on fuzzy algorithms has strong adaptability and high control performance, providing an effective solution for soccer robots to track targets in dynamic environments.

articleTitle: Design of Multifunctional Integrated Real-Time Traffic Supervision System
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 5th International Conference on Power, Electronics and Computer Applications (ICPECA)
abstract: This study focuses on the intelligence of urban traffic management, aiming to solve the increasingly severe urban traffic congestion and safety problems by integrating computer vision, deep learning technology, and Internet of Things technology. Based on the Faster R-CNN algorithm, a multifunctional integrated real-time traffic monitoring system was developed to achieve core functions such as traffic flow monitoring, pedestrian and non motorized vehicle detection, illegal behavior recognition, traffic sign recognition, and traffic accident detection. The system uses Raspberry Pi 4B as the main control chip, transmits data through Bluetooth module, and utilizes FREETROS operating system to achieve coordinated operation of tasks. The experimental results show that the system can recognize traffic targets with high accuracy (mAP50 is 56.3 %) and issue timely alarm information when a traffic accident is detected, demonstrating the effectiveness and reliability of the system in improving traffic management efficiency and ensuring traffic safety. This study provides new solutions and technical support for building a traffic management system for smart cities.

articleTitle: A Collaborative Change Detection Network Based on Feature Pyramids
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 5th International Conference on Power, Electronics and Computer Applications (ICPECA)
abstract: The application of high-resolution satellite images in deep learning-based change detection methods has become increasingly popular. However, the down-sampling and cropping strategies deployed to fit the GPU memory constraint often result in incomplete semantic information and loss of fine details. This paper proposes a collaborative network based on feature pyramids, which enables networks to learn local and global features from cropped and down-sampled image patches. A feature-sharing mechanism is also introduced to fuse global features and local features. We evaluated the network on the LEVIR and S2Looking datasets by comparing it with some representative change detection networks. Comparative experiments show that the proposed network performs better in multi-scale change detection, improving precision by 2.69% on the LEVIR-CD dataset, and improving precision and recall by 6.83% and 2.68% on the S2Looking dataset, respectively.

articleTitle: Framework Design of Fault Diagnosis System Based on Improved LSTM Networks
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 5th International Conference on Power, Electronics and Computer Applications (ICPECA)
abstract: In the current era of high industrialisation, fault diagnosis of complex industrial systems is facing unprecedented challenges. Traditional fault diagnosis methods based on physical models and signal processing gradually show their limitations, especially when facing nonlinear and nonsmooth signals as well as fusion of multi-source information. In this paper, we propose a framework design of a fault diagnosis system based on a long short-term memory network (LSTM) with improved attention mechanism. The system employs high-precision sensors to collect real-time operating signals from key components, and analyses and diagnoses these signals through a deep learning model to quickly and accurately determine whether there is a fault in the equipment and provide detailed fault type and location information. In particular, an attention mechanism is introduced to enhance the model's focus on key features in the fault signals, thereby improving the accuracy and reliability of fault diagnosis. Experimental results show that the proposed LSTM-Attention network performs well on the bearing fault dataset and achieves high classification accuracy.

articleTitle: Strategic Research on the Health Management Data Storage Mechanism Integrating Blockchain Technology Based on the Improved PBFT Consensus Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 5th International Conference on Power, Electronics and Computer Applications (ICPECA)
abstract: At present, the existing databases in medical institutions are characterized by singularity and centralization in storage methods. This makes it difficult to guarantee the security, integrity, and traceability of electronic medical data, thus posing a threat to patients' medical privacy. Although some studies have proposed data security storage solutions based on cloud storage and the like, such solutions rely on a completely trustworthy third-party to ensure the reliability of interactions. To address the above-mentioned problems, this paper proposes a decentralized health management data storage mechanism by integrating blockchain technology based on the improved PBFT consensus algorithm. This mechanism uses the improved PBFT consensus algorithm and the optimized Hash encryption algorithm to securely and effectively store health management data in a distributed database, ensuring the integrity and traceability of the data. At the same time, a new data interaction system is designed to prevent direct interaction between the third-party and the database, preventing untrustworthy third-parties from maliciously damaging the data and ensuring data security. In addition, through access control and the Lucene retrieval mechanism, patient privacy is protected and rapid retrieval of health management data is achieved. Experimental analysis shows that compared with algorithms such as Proof of Work (POW) and Delegated Proof of Stake (DPOS), the improved PBFT consensus algorithm endows the medical blockchain system with better stability and throughput. Compared with the ordinary database interaction method, the designed data interaction system effectively prevents direct operations on the database and has good security and anti-tampering properties. Experimental data indicates that the decentralized health management data storage system constructed by integrating blockchain technology based on the improved PBFT consensus algorithm realizes the secure storage, traceability, and anti-tampering of health management data, overcomes the problems of centralized storage, non-traceability, and vulnerability to attacks of health management data, and lays a foundation for the in-depth application and development of blockchain technology in the medical information field.

articleTitle: A New Multiple Agricultural Machinery Scheduling via a Genetic Algorithm Improved by Large Neighborhood Search Method
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 5th International Conference on Power, Electronics and Computer Applications (ICPECA)
abstract: Aiming at the problem that the commonly used scheduling algorithm in the process of intelligent scheduling of agricultural machinery are easy to fall into local optimum, a multiple agricultural machinery scheduling operation method with a genetic algorithm improved by large neighborhood search method is proposed. To begin with, focusing on the shortcomings of high cost and inefficient of agricultural machinery scheduling, an agricultural machinery scheduling model with a time window is constructed, with the optimization goal of least total operating cost. Subsequently, a genetic algorithm improved by large neighborhood search algorithm is designed. Through selection, crossover, mutation and local search, better solutions are continuously sought. By adding adaptability to the crossover and mutation processes and simultaneously improving the large neighborhood search operator, a more efficient and flexible search for the optimal solution is achieved. Finally, comparative experiments with six commonly used algorithms are carried out based on real data sets. The experimental results show that even if the number of farmlands increases, the scheduling cost of the proposed algorithm still maintains a significant advantage. When the number of farmlands is 17, 27 and 37, the total cost is reduced by an average of 171.40, 305.28 and 460.39 CNY respectively. Moreover, the advantages of this algorithm in terms of convergence results and speed are more prominent.

articleTitle: Autonomous Exploration Algorithms for Unmanned Aerial Vehicles in Unknown Environments
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 5th International Conference on Power, Electronics and Computer Applications (ICPECA)
abstract: Autonomous exploration in GNSS-free indoor scenarios is a hot issue in UAV research. Existing autonomous exploration algorithms for UAVs have been able to run smoothly on small on-board computers and accomplish tasks while meeting the requirements of exploration efficiency and accuracy. However, most of the current algorithms fail to solve the problem of duplicate routes caused by the fact that “corner clusters” near obstacles and “closed-loop clusters” wrapped by known regions are not prioritized for exploration. In this paper, we summarize the common characteristics of these clusters and propose a new FIS structure, which adds the data of the number of voxels in the cluster, the plane size of the voxels, and the ratio of the number of voxels in the cluster located in the effective distance field on the basis of the original FIS structure, and gives the corresponding judgment method. Based on the FUEL Planner autonomous exploration algorithm, an improved algorithm to drive rotorcraft for autonomous exploration, based on the first layer of the algorithm to solve the global path with the traveler algorithm, we add a sequence of clusters with greater priority to place the “edge clusters” and “closed-loop clusters”, and prioritize the access to this sequence. “The sequence of clusters in this sequence is accessed first, and then the clusters solved by the original FUEL algorithm using the traveler algorithm are accessed. The algorithm is simulated and verified against the original FUEL Planner algorithm.

articleTitle: Dynamic State Monitoring for Substation Operation Safety: A Kalman Filter-Based Approach
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 5th International Conference on Power, Electronics and Computer Applications (ICPECA)
abstract: With the increase in the complexity of power systems, the security and reliability of substation operations have become key issues in grid operation. In this paper, a dynamic environment sensing and operation calibration method based on multi-source data fusion is proposed. By integrating temperature, humidity, vibration and other sensor data, the denoising and fusion processing of multi-source data is realized by using Ensemble Kalman Filter (EnKF) technology to monitor the substation environment and equipment status in real time. For accidental anomaly data points, this paper adopts Hampel filter for filtering, and combines the improved DBSCAN algorithm to detect the continuity anomaly data set, effectively identifying the defects and faults of the equipment. The method improves the accuracy and real-time performance of substation fault detection, and can provide strong support for the safe operation and operation optimization of the power grid.

articleTitle: Design and Implementation of a Video Secure Communication System Based on High-Dimensional Hyperchaos
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 5th International Conference on Power, Electronics and Computer Applications (ICPECA)
abstract: This paper presents a scheme of video security based on high dimensional hyperchaos. A new high dimensional hyperchaos mapping model is proposed to generate key sequences and encrypt video data. By performing pixel-level scrambling and block-level encryption on video frames, the confidentiality of video data is enhanced, and the video quality and real-time transmission are guaranteed. Compared with traditional video encryption algorithms (such as AES), this system has higher encryption strength and anti-cracking capabilities. Experiments show that the proposed scheme has good performance in encryption, video quality, encryption and decryption, and anti-interference capability. Specifically, compared with AES encryption, the anti-cracking time of this system is improved by about 30%, and the encrypted video quality is almost lossless, which can ensure real-time transmission. Under different bandwidth and network conditions, the system can adaptively adjust the encryption strength and decryption speed to ensure efficient and secure transmission of video data.

articleTitle: Research on Noise Suppression and Signal Enhancement in Electricity Price Anomaly Detection
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 5th International Conference on Power, Electronics and Computer Applications (ICPECA)
abstract: As the key economic index of electricity market, electricity price is directly affected by the change of supply and demand balance. However, there are often various noises in the actual electricity market data, which makes the detection of electricity price anomalies difficult. Through effective noise suppression and signal enhancement, this paper proposes a method called PRO-WOA, which combines whale optimization algorithm and wavelet transform to achieve noise suppression and signal enhancement in power price anomaly detection. Taking the actual power trading data of a province in 2022 as the research object, we conducted comparative experiments on different models. The results show that PRO-WOA performs well in forecasting accuracy and real-time performance, significantly outperforming other comparison models.

articleTitle: Semi-Supervised Object Detection with Adaptive Pseudo-Label Mining
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 5th International Conference on Power, Electronics and Computer Applications (ICPECA)
abstract: To address the problem of threshold selection and scale imbalance in semi-supervised object detection, we presents an adaptive pseudo-labeling mining method to tackle the aforementioned issues. Firstly, the pseudo-labels were divided into three types: negative pseudo-labels, uncertain pseudo-labels and positive pseudo-labels, and the Gaussian mixture model was used to set a threshold for each type of pseudo-labels, and the pseudo-label threshold was dynamically adjusted to solve the problem of fixed threshold. Then, the negative samples in the uncertain pseudo-labels are further identified and mined by the adaptive pseudo-label mining module to extract more high-quality pseudo-labels for model training. In order to resolve the issue of scale imbalance, this paper proposes a strategy combining dual Region Generative Network (DRPN) and Upsampling based on feature Content-aware reorganization (CARAFE). The experimental findings demonstrate that the mAP value of the proposed method on the 5% and 10% labels of the Microsoft COCO dataset is increased by 0.5 and 1.1, respectively. This outcome validates the efficacy and superiority of the proposed method in the domain of semi-supervised object detection.

articleTitle: Ensemble Learning-Based Electricity Theft Detection: Combining Deep & Cross Network and Transformer
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 5th International Conference on Power, Electronics and Computer Applications (ICPECA)
abstract: Eletheft, as a core issue of non-technical losses, has become more complex with the emergence of new network attack methods. Studies indicate that machine learning models relying solely on raw data have limitations when handling complex and covert composite attacks. In response, this study undertakes a comprehensive approach, proposing an ensemble learning-based DCN-Transformer weighted algorithm to address this challenge. We begin by manually extracting electricity consumption and environmental features and use Pearson correlation to quantify their relationships and time-lag effects. The DCN and Transformer models are then independently trained and optimized, with key parameters fine-tuned using grid search to enhance detection performance. Finally, during the integration phase, the prediction results of the two models are intelligently weighted and merged to construct a comprehensive prediction score. Our experimental results, which are the product of this thorough approach, show that considering environmental factors improves model performance, achieving an accuracy of 93.9%, precision of 92.8%, recall of 93.8%, F1 score of 91.8%, and a false detection rate of only 6%. Compared to other algorithms, our proposed method demonstrates significant advantages, further validating the thoroughness of our study.

articleTitle: Research on Automatic Driving System Based on End-to-End and Real-Time Path Planning
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 5th International Conference on Power, Electronics and Computer Applications (ICPECA)
abstract: With the development of autonomous driving technology, visual perception systems face challenges in target detection and localization tasks in complex traffic scenes, deep learning provides new ways to solve this problem, but single-phase and two-phase target detection algorithms need to balance speed and accuracy. In this paper, we study the related work of machine vision in the field of autonomous driving, based on which we propose path planning methods based on multiple neural networks, including CNN, RNN, Transformer and Occupancy Network, etc., and design an integrated framework to make the perception and path planning modules work closely together. The experimental results show that in the end-to-end model performance comparison, the CNN-LSTM-Transformer model converges fast and has the lowest loss and error in the validation set, and has the highest path prediction accuracy and robustness; the evaluation of the real-time path planning algorithm reveals that it has a high real-time performance with an average time delay of only 0.0003 seconds, an average mean square error of 0.0081, an average absolute error of 0.0723, and an average path length of 0.0081, and an average path length of 0.0723. The average mean square error is 0.0081, the average absolute error is 0.0723, and the average path length is 12.3465, so the path quality is good. Future research can further optimize the algorithm to improve the model adaptability and detection efficiency, in order to promote the development of automatic driving technology.

articleTitle: Enhanced Dynamic Interactive Multi-View Memory Network for Utterance-Level Sentiment Recognition
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 5th International Conference on Power, Electronics and Computer Applications (ICPECA)
abstract: Multimodal models are one of the keys to enhancing emotion recognition in conversation. Videos, audios, and texts in the dialogue can help analyze and improve the emotional expression of the interlocutors. Existing emotion recognition models often struggle to effectively capture complex contextual information and nuanced emotional tones, making it difficult to leverage dialogue information effectively. How to effectively integrate multimodal features to further understand emotional expressions in dialogues remains a challenge. To address the aforementioned issues, an Enhanced Dynamic Interactive Multi-view Memory Network for Utterance-level Sentiment Recognition (EDIMMN-USR) is proposed. Firstly, dynamically capture cross-modal interactive information through a multi-view attention network. Secondly, hierarchical gated recurrent units integrated with feature fusion and Temporal Convolutional Networks are utilized to learn long-range dependencies and complex contextual emotions for individual interlocutors. Finally, bidirectional gated recurrent units and a memory network are used to model the global dialogue, capturing complex contextual information across multiple turns of dialogue. Experimental results on IEMOCAP and MELD datasets showed that the accuracy of EDIMMN-USR was improved by 1.87% and 4.7% respectively.

articleTitle: Cross-Session EEG Motor Imagery Classification Method Based on Transfer Learning
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 5th International Conference on Power, Electronics and Computer Applications (ICPECA)
abstract: Motor imagery (MI) electroencephalogram (EEG) signals exhibit cross-session variability, which hinders traditional EEG classification models from achieving satisfactory performance in cross-session EEG data classification. Therefore, further adjustments and optimizations are needed. To resolve this problem, the research develops a transfer learning-based approach for cross-session motor imagery EEG classification. To comprehensively analyze EEG data, this study introduces an attention-optimized separable CNN framework for multi-domain feature extraction (spectral, spatial, and temporal). In parallel, supervised learning is applied to reduce the classification error of source domain data. Meanwhile, transfer learning is leveraged to enhance the alignment of feature representations between source and target domains, enabling the training of a neural network capable of effectively processing cross-session EEG datasets. Finally, the proposed algorithm is compared with several selected advanced algorithms and evaluated on the publicly available 2008 BCI Competition IV 2a dataset. The results show that without any manual feature extraction, the proposed cross-session EEG motor imagery classification method based on transfer learning achieves an average accuracy of 73.1% and a Kappa value of 64.8% for the four-class classification dataset.

articleTitle: DAMOT: A Novel Algorithm for High-Speed Target Sparse Flight Trajectory Interpolation
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 5th International Conference on Power, Electronics and Computer Applications (ICPECA)
abstract: High-speed target flight trajectories typically involve extensive temporal and spatial ranges, with data frequently missing in both discrete and continuous segments. Missing data lead to overall trajectory sparsity, and hindering the development of downstream applications. Most existing algorithms primarily address discrete missing data, lacking the capability to interpolate trajectories through continuous missing segments. To address this issue, we propose a Transformer-based decoupled adaptive learning multi-headed output algorithm (DAMOT) for sparse flight trajectory interpolation. DAMOT leverages the self-attention mechanism to learn inferential relationships among individual trajectory points and incorporates observed data to predict missing states. Using a multi-head attention framework with multi-head outputs, it decouples multi–dimensional attributes—such as latitude, longitude, altitude, and speed—to reduce systematic errors in attribute–specific interpolations. A boundary prediction layer further enhances spatial constraints for missing spans by leveraging boundary point information. Meanwhile, an adaptive loss function dynamically adjusts the model's focus during different training stages, improving convergence. Experimental results demonstrate that DAMOT's span–masking training method offers greater robustness to continuous missing data, and that its architecture and loss function achieve higher interpolation accuracy compared to existing approaches.

articleTitle: Study on YSR Model for Detecting the Mandibular Strap of Safety Helmet
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 5th International Conference on Power, Electronics and Computer Applications (ICPECA)
abstract: In the field of public infrastructure development, safety helmet is an important guarantee for the life safety of front-line construction workers. Aiming at the problem of safety helmet wearing standards, we proposes a YSR safety helmet jaw band detection model based on (YOLOv7, image superresolution reconstruction (SA-SRGAN) and classification network model (SA-ResNet). The algorithm firstly locates and extracts the helmet in the monitoring image based on YOLOv7 network model. Secondly, SA-SRGAN network with attention mechanism is used to improve the image resolution. Finally, SAResNet, which introduces attention mechanism, is used to identify the wearing standard of the helmet jaw strap. At the same time, the data set of construction site is made to verify the reliability of the proposed algorithm. Findings from the experiments indicate that the YOLOv7 model boasts an average precision of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbf{9 8. 7 8 \%}$</tex>. The reconstruction effect of SA-SRGAN model was the best, and its subjective evaluation standard score was 3.69. The classification accuracy of SA-ResNet was 98.83 %. Therefore, based on monitoring images, our method can effectively identify whether the helmet jaw strap is worn properly, with its recognition accuracy fulfilling the requirements for construction site monitoring.

articleTitle: Intelligent Monocular Visual Dynamic Detection Method for Safe Distance of Hot Work Operation
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 5th International Conference on Power, Electronics and Computer Applications (ICPECA)
abstract: The present paper proposes a monocular visual distance detection model, namely DID-CAYOLO, to supervise the irregular operation of workers in construction sites. Visual information is collected using a single CCD sensor, and the YOLOv7 network model is enhanced with CA attention mechanism to improve the accuracy of identifying hot areas, operators, and equipment. Two-dimensional position information of the target is gathered and inverse perspective transformation is performed using a security ranging measurement algorithm to obtain three-dimensional spatial position information and measure distances. Experimental verification demonstrates that the proposed monocular safe distance detection algorithm, DID-CAYOLO, can accurately calculate distances between identified targets. Field tests show an average target detection accuracy of 99.14 % on hot operation datasets with a single image reasoning time of 27.4 ms and ranging accuracy within <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\pm 0.11 \ \mathrm{m}$</tex>. This approach fulfills safety distance detection and warning requirements in industrial sites while effectively preventing safety risks associated with hot operations.

articleTitle: Target Detection Comparison Between YOLO and Transformer
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 5th International Conference on Power, Electronics and Computer Applications (ICPECA)
abstract: Respiratory-induced tumor motion poses a significant challenge to the efficacy of precision radiotherapy, particularly in scenarios requiring high-accuracy real-time detecting. This paper systematically compares the performance of two deep learning architectures, Transformer and YOLOv8, for surface marker detecting, with the goal of generating realtime respiratory signals, thus modelling or predicting tumor motion. Transformer demonstrated superior detecting accuracy, while limited by its latency and lack of lightweight design, while YOLOv8 excelled in real-time performance and efficiency but fell short in precision. These observations highlight the complementary strengths of the two models, suggesting a hybrid approach that integrates the accuracy of Transformer with the efficiency of YOLOv8 to address the challenges of tumor motion management in precision radiotherapy.

articleTitle: Main Circuit Solutions and Control Principles for Grid-connected Power Generation of Wind Turbines
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 5th International Conference on Power, Electronics and Computer Applications (ICPECA)
abstract: In recent years, wind energy has assumed growing significance within the energy domain. It enables the power generation industry to reduce its reliance on traditional fossil fuels, with approximately 106 megawatts of wind energy on Earth being amenable to continuous exploitation. This study centers on the grid-connected power generation of wind turbines, presenting a comprehensive analysis of its main circuit solutions and control principles. For main circuit solutions, the topological structures of power converters employed in grid-connected wind power generation are elaborated in detail. This encompasses an exploration of the characteristics, application scenarios, and a comparison of the pros and cons of different converter types. Moreover, in-depth research is conducted on energy storage systems in wind power applications, analyzing the application modalities and effects of diverse energy storage technologies in the context of wind power generation. Additionally, high-voltage direct-current (HVDC) transmission lines utilized in grid-connected wind power are examined, elucidating their pivotal role in the long-distance and large-capacity transmission of wind energy. Regarding control principles, the maximum power point tracking method is principally introduced, elucidating how it attains efficient wind energy capture through precise control. Simultaneously, extensive discussions are held on wind conditions, wind energy potential estimation, the configuration and design of wind energy conversion systems, and the characteristics of wind turbines themselves, as these factors are inextricably linked to the formulation of control strategies. To guarantee the power quality of grid-connected electricity, power-smoothing methods are comprehensively expounded. Furthermore, the requirements and impacts of international grid codes on the control of grid-connected power generation of wind turbines are delved into deeply. Through a comprehensive literature analysis, this review endeavors to offer researchers, designers, manufacturers, and engineers engaged in grid-connected wind power generation research a key-topic synopsis and a summary of existing technologies in the realm of main circuit solutions and control principles, thereby functioning as a highly practical guide within this field.

articleTitle: Optimization of Real-Time Dynamic Gesture Recognition Based on Multi-Scale Spatio-Temporal Residual Graph Convolutional Neural Networks
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 5th International Conference on Power, Electronics and Computer Applications (ICPECA)
abstract: The challenge of real-time dynamic gesture recognition is how to accurately locate the gestures in the video and take into account the real-time and accuracy in the recognition process. Aiming at the problem of dynamic gesture recognition in video, this paper proposes a dynamic gesture recognition method based on the multi-scale spatio-temporal residual graph convolution. The convolution module based on spatio-temporal residual graph is used to capture the motion information at different time and spatial scales, expand the receptive field of spatio-temporal dimension, and use the residual structure system to process hierarchically. The dynamic gesture recognition algorithm is designed by using the characteristics of time series, gesture category, gesture coordinates and gesture area to complete the dynamic gesture recognition. The gesture recognition performance of the model is tested under simple and complex background. Under the same level model, the performance of this model has certain advantages.

articleTitle: Research on Network Security Protection Technologies of Distributed Power Dispatch Control System on Main Station Side
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 5th International Conference on Power, Electronics and Computer Applications (ICPECA)
abstract: The integration of distributed power sources into modern power grids has introduced significant network security challenges to Distributed Power Dispatch Control Systems (DPDCS). These systems are critical for managing distributed energy resources (DERs), requiring real-time communication and coordination between control centers and distributed terminals. However, the openness and interconnectivity of DPDCS expose them to a variety of network security risks, including unauthorized access, malicious software attacks, and data breaches. This paper addresses the network security protection technology for the master side of DPDCS, focusing on software vulnerabilities, protocol interactions, device control, and security event analysis. We propose comprehensive solutions for network security recognition, vulnerability detection, information interaction security, and device state management. By employing state-of-the-art methods such as anomaly detection, automated vulnerability scanning, and multi-dimensional data analytics, this study aims to establish a robust foundation for securing distributed power dispatch systems. The implementation of these solutions is crucial for ensuring the stability and security of DPDCS in open interactive business environments.

articleTitle: Mechanical Electrical Automation Control System Based on PLC Technology
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 5th International Conference on Power, Electronics and Computer Applications (ICPECA)
abstract: In response to the increasingly complex mechanical and electrical automation control needs in modern industry, this paper studies a mechanical and electrical automation control system design scheme based on PLC (Programmable Logic Controller) technology. This study first starts with the system architecture and builds an industrial automation control system, including power supply, input/output modules, control logic, human-computer interaction, communication and safety modules. The system core uses Siemens S7-1500 PLC; the input/output module uses photoelectric isolation technology to improve signal stability; the control logic module integrates the adaptive PID (Proportion Integral Differential) algorithm; the human-computer interface realizes real-time data and alarm display based on the WinCC platform. The communication module uses the PROFINET network enhanced by TSN (Time-Sensitive Networking); the safety module is designed with emergency stop and light curtain sensor mechanisms. During the test, the performance of the system is verified through hardware-in-the-loop (HIL) simulation technology, and the stability and parameter sensitivity of the control algorithm are analyzed using the gray box test method. Experimental results show that in the position control experiment, the maximum absolute error of the system is 0.1 mm, the velocity fluctuation rate is controlled within <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\pm 0.3 \%$</tex>, and the force control error is maintained within <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\pm 0.2 ~\mathrm{N}$</tex>. Under a variety of load and environmental conditions, the system exhibits excellent dynamic response and robustness. The research results show that the PLC control system designed in this paper has strong adaptability and efficiency in industrial automation control applications, and can effectively meet the needs of modern industry for high-precision control and multi-device collaboration.

articleTitle: Application of Multimodal Deep Learning Algorithm in Image and Text Fusion Recognition
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 5th International Conference on Power, Electronics and Computer Applications (ICPECA)
abstract: With the explosive growth of multimedia data, how to effectively extract information from images and texts and realize the integration of the two has become a research hotspot. This paper discusses the application of multimodal deep learning algorithms in this field to enhance the correlation between image and text features, especially by introducing the cross-modal attention mechanism (CAM). In this paper, a multi-modal encoder-decoder model based on Transformer architecture is proposed, which uses the Self-Attention Mechanism to effectively solve the problem of long-distance dependence and aligns the semantic space of images and texts. In order to overcome the imbalance of training data, a weighted loss function was designed to ensure that the samples of each category could be fully learned. Finally, the robustness and generalization ability of the system are further enhanced by optimizing the configuration of model parameters.

articleTitle: Unmanned Vessel Path Planning Strategy Based on Improved Bidirectional RRT Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 5th International Conference on Power, Electronics and Computer Applications (ICPECA)
abstract: In this paper, we propose a strategy based on an improved bidirectional RRT algorithm for solving the path planning problem of unmanned vessels. Compared with the traditional RRT algorithm, there are many advantages of bidirectional RRT, and this paper carries out further improvement on the basis of bidirectional RRT: the distance field technique is adopted to realize the bias sampling near the obstacle boundary, so as to improve the probability of finding the connecting paths; and the cubic spline interpolation is used to smooth the generated paths to ensure that they conform to the actual kinematic constraints and to improve the feasibility of execution. These two improvements can serve to accelerate the path planning speed and optimize the overall route. After experimental verification, the improved two-way RRT algorithm is significantly better than the traditional RRT algorithm in terms of planning efficiency, and is able to quickly and accurately generate safe and optimized paths for unmanned vessels.

articleTitle: Sensor Placement Based on Cellular Communication Systems
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 5th International Conference on Power, Electronics and Computer Applications (ICPECA)
abstract: This paper presents a novel approach for optimizing sensor placement within a designated area, leveraging a combination of cellular communication systems and feed-forward neural networks to streamline the selection process for operators. Initially, a modified hill-climbing algorithm, a form of local search, is implemented to generate preliminary data for sensor positioning. However, to prevent the algorithm from converging on local optima, a simulated annealing algorithm is subsequently employed to validate and refine the results. During the construction phase of the cellular communication system, flaws were detected in the evaluation metrics when using Modal Assurance Criterion (MAC) and singular value ratios, which led to the adoption of a feed-forward neural network. This neural network is utilized for both further optimization and a more accurate assessment of the sensor distribution. The study highlights the seamless integration of cellular communication systems with local search methods and underscores the significant improvements in optimization achieved through the use of neural networks. Ultimately, the research successfully develops a method for determining the optimal sensor positions, providing a robust solution for the effective deployment of cellular sensors in complex environments.

articleTitle: Rapid Precise Time and Frequency Transfer Using GPS and Galileo Multi-Frequency Precise Point Positioning with Ambiguity Resolution
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 5th International Conference on Power, Electronics and Computer Applications (ICPECA)
abstract: Precise Point Positioning (PPP) has become a versatile and competitive technique for time and frequency transfer across various fields. However, PPP's long convergence time, caused by slow satellite geometry changes and low pseudorange accuracy, limits its use in real-time time and frequency transfer. This study investigates the impact of GPS and Galileo multi-frequency PPP ambiguity resolution (PPPAR) on time and frequency transfer stability and convergence. We established four time links and evaluated six system and frequency combinations. The results show that multiconstellation and multi-frequency approaches significantly improve short-term stability. They reduce the standard deviation of epoch differences by 10% to 25%. The modified Allan deviation (MDEV) results indicate that multiconstellation and multi-frequency approaches enhance frequency stability by 15 % to 30 % over a 90 s averaging period. While long-term stability remains influenced by satellite clock offsets and environmental factors, multi-constellation and multi-frequency PPP-AR proved to be a robust solution for rapid convergence and enhanced short-time stability, making it particularly suitable for real-time applications.

articleTitle: Research on the Application of Multi-Channel Display Technology in Virtual Scene Image Generation
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 5th International Conference on Power, Electronics and Computer Applications (ICPECA)
abstract: This study proposes an innovative algorithm based on DCNN and multi-channel image fusion, aiming to improve the quality and efficiency of virtual scene image generation. The algorithm extracts depth information and texture features in virtual scenes through DCNN, and combines multi-channel image fusion technology to optimize and fuse the information of different image channels (such as color, depth, normal, etc.), thereby significantly improving the image rendering effect. Through adaptive weight adjustment and image fusion strategy, the image detail performance is optimized, especially in scenes with complex lighting and rich textures, the rendering quality is significantly improved. Experimental results show that the image generation system based on this algorithm improves image quality by 15%, rendering speed by 25%, and computing resource consumption by 20%. When processing highly complex virtual scenes, the system can achieve real-time rendering and meet the performance requirements of VR and AR applications. This study provides a new and efficient solution for image generation in virtual reality and augmented reality, and demonstrates the great potential of combining multi-channel display technology with deep learning in improving rendering effects.

articleTitle: Model-Free Robust Height Trajectory Tracking Control for Nonlinear LAVs
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 5th International Conference on Power, Electronics and Computer Applications (ICPECA)
abstract: Faced with the nonlinear low altitude vehicle (LAV) trajectory tracking control problem, in order to track the desired trajectory more accurately and respond to the changes of inputs faster, this paper proposes a model-free adaptive control method under the data-driven framework, which solves the problem of controlling the flight altitude of low altitude vehicles under the scenario of Dos network attack. In this paper, the data mapping of LAV is established based on the tight-format dynamic linear programming technique under the compressed mapping criterion. Firstly, the simulation of normal flight control is carried out for low altitude vehicles with different flight parameters, and then the simulation of cyber-attacks under three different scenarios, namely, momentary communication interruption, temporal communication interruption, and probabilistic interruption of communication is carried out, and it is verified that the model has a faster trajectory speed, a more accurate trajectory precision and a better stability.

articleTitle: Application of Deep Learning in Natural Language Processing Algorithm for User Service
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 5th International Conference on Power, Electronics and Computer Applications (ICPECA)
abstract: Natural language processing (NLP) is becoming more and more widely used in the field of user services. This paper discusses the innovative application of NLP algorithm based on deep learning in improving user service quality, and focuses on several key algorithms and their optimization methods. Firstly, by introducing pre-trained language models such as BERT and GPT-3, the efficient understanding of user services and the generation of responses are realized, which greatly improves the accuracy and fluency of the dialogue system. Secondly, for the intent recognition task in the user service, a multi-head attention mechanism based on Transformer architecture is proposed, which enhances the ability of the model to capture long-distance dependencies and enables the system to analyze the user's intent more accurately. In addition, in order to solve the challenge of context understanding in multi-turn dialogue, we designed a memory-enhanced recurrent neural network (RNN) with a fusion memory network, which can maintain and update the dialogue state in multiple rounds of interaction, so as to provide a coherent service experience. Finally, this paper discusses the challenges and solutions in the process of model deployment, real-time inference efficiency and data privacy protection, and looks forward to the application prospects of supervised learning and adaptive transfer learning.

articleTitle: Research on X-Ray Image Detection Algorithm Based on YOLO-MCA
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 5th International Conference on Power, Electronics and Computer Applications (ICPECA)
abstract: A novel object detection method for X-ray image detection is realized by using the YOLO-MCA algorithm. This algorithm utilizes a convolutional neural network (CNN) to perform powerful feature extraction, and the combined nature of two-stage and single-stage object detection algorithms is aimed toward increasing mostly the efficiency and accuracy. Progressive development in the YOLO family with added optimization in the structure of the network builds a good base by intelligent design of anchors and precise border regression for object detection. In this study, a YOLO-MCA architecture has been constructed, putting emphasis on increasing the sensitivity and adaptability of the network toward various targets through the use of a multi-channel attention (MCA) mechanism. The precise design of the training module and the appropriately coordinated detection module make it very effective, and experimental data shows that it is very helpful in improving the recognition of complex shapes in X-ray images. The experimental results show that the YOLO-MCA algorithm has high performance in terms of accuracy and speed, which provides new ideas and potential application value for future medical image analysis.

articleTitle: “Cropmaster” - Real-Time Coordination of Multirobot Systems for Autonomous Crop Harvesting: Design and Implementation
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 5th International Conference on Power, Electronics and Computer Applications (ICPECA)
abstract: The CropMaster is an autonomous rover system designed to enhance Scotch Bonnet production by improving disease management, crop sorting, autonomous navigation, and real-time environmental monitoring. Equipped with sensors to measure sunlight, humidity, pH, NPK content, and soil moisture, the rover securely transmits analyzed data to a web-based dashboard. LIDAR technology enables efficient autonomous navigation, allowing the rover to move around fields and avoid obstacles. The MQTT protocol facilitates communication between multiple rovers, preventing duplicate measurements and ensuring data is sent to the dashboard for comprehensive data collection across large areas. TensorFlow's machine learning models allow the rover to accurately assess crop health and detect early-stage diseases, followed by automated pesticide and fertilizer application through a spraying system. To maintain reliability, the rover's operations, including data transfer and task execution, are continuously monitored for Quality of Service (QoS). All collected data is stored in the cloud for long-term access. Built with a lightweight aluminum and plastic chassis and robotic arms, the rover is designed for adaptability and operational efficiency, aiming to improve crop management and increase yields across extensive agricultural fields.

articleTitle: Frequency-Domain Pruning Based on Inter-Channel Perspective
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 5th International Conference on Power, Electronics and Computer Applications (ICPECA)
abstract: Filter pruning significantly enhances the deployment efficiency of deep convolutional models by reducing their resource demands. Previous works primarily focus on spatial domain pruning, eliminating redundant filters from an intra-channel perspective while ignoring the substitutability between filters. To tackle this problem, we introduce an innovative pruning method that transforms feature maps from the spatial domain to the frequency domain for analysis, with pruning performed based on the inter-channel substitutability score to rank filters accordingly. Our comprehensive experiments on CIFAR-10 and ImageNet confirm the proposed method's efficiency in compressing networks. For instance, on CIFAR-10, our approach decreases FLOPs by 58.10% and 71.8% for VGG-16-BN and ResNet-110, respectively, concurrently enhancing Top-1 accuracy by 0.32% and 0.09%. On ImageNet, it reduces FLOPs by 44.8%, cuts parameters by 40.8%, and boosts Top-1 accuracy by 0.12% for ResNet-50. Furthermore, ablation analyses validate the efficiency of individual components within our methodology.

articleTitle: Meta-Learning Framework for Effective Few Shot Time Series Prediction
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 5th International Conference on Power, Electronics and Computer Applications (ICPECA)
abstract: Few shot time series forecasting is a significant challenge in fields such as healthcare, IoT, and finance, where data scarcity limits the effectiveness of traditional predictive models. Conventional methods often struggle to capture complex temporal patterns and generalize effectively with limited training data. To address this issue, this paper presents a novel meta-learning-based framework designed to enhance forecasting accuracy and adaptability in data-constrained scenarios. The framework leverages knowledge from related tasks through meta-training, enabling rapid adaptation to new tasks with minimal data. This work integrates attention mechanisms to identify salient temporal dependencies and task-specific adaptation layers to improve flexibility and handle task heterogeneity. By extracting and transferring shared patterns across tasks, the framework achieves robust generalization and efficient learning. Comprehensive experiments conducted on diverse real-world datasets demonstrate significant improvements in prediction accuracy and adaptability compared to traditional approaches and meta-learning baselines. The results highlight the proposed method's ability to generalize across domains, offering a practical solution for scenarios characterized by dynamic environments and limited data availability. This work underscores the potential of meta-learning to advance time series forecasting, supporting its broader application in resource-constrained and high-impact fields such as personalized healthcare, predictive maintenance, and financial analysis.
